title: Annotatio VI §.II: Damnationes of non-fundamental opinions in the Epitome — against Lutheric brethren and Reformeds
pass_a_gloss: further, joined promiscuously with Damnations of opposing opinions, however most innocuous, true or false, certainly not fundamental: such damnations as are read in great number in the Epitome of the articles concerning which Controversies have arisen among the Theologians of the Augsburg Confession — laid both against some opinions of the Lutheric Brethren called by the same name of Luther, and against more of the Reformeds — for example against these:
pass_b_english: It is also promiscuously joined to damnations of opposing opinions — however harmless, whether true or false, and certainly not fundamental.

In the Epitome of articles on controversies among Augsburg Confession theologians, such damnations abound — against some opinions of Luther’s own-named brethren, and against more on the Reformed side — for example these:
source_text: praeterea cum Damnationibus opinionum adversantium, utut maximè innocuarum, verarum, seu falsarum, certè non fundamentalium, conjunctum promiscuè: quales damnationes in Epitome articulorum, de quibus Controversiae ortae sunt inter Theologos August. Confessionis, quam plurimae leguntur, tàm in opiniones Fratrum Luthericorum, ab eodem Lutheri nomine appellatorum, nonnullas, quam in Reformatorum plures latas, e. g. in has,
notes: Damnationes non-fundamental; Epitome vs Lutheric brethren + Reformeds.
